how: experiments/t88-substack/paste_payload_lane.js in the desktop app's built-in browser, where his Substack is signed in: each draft's title checked, the body cleared with real keystrokes (ctrl+a, Delete) and checked empty, the script and the payload fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at the commit and their SHA-256 checked, then pasted; Substack's 'Saved' seen, and the editor reloaded and its words counted again; then the secret preview link in the paid subscriber view (tools/humanization/substack_secret_link.js) opened and its text checked (tools/humanization/substack_rendered_check.js). Never published.
first_paste: At 2b7f7e67 the payloads had the standard swap's straight quote marks. Substack's editor curled all of them on paste (821 curly marks in draft A) and three double ones after an opening bracket the wrong way, bringing back typos he fixed in turn 117: (”What would Jesus do?”, (”You hated that coat”), (”Once upon a time…”. So make_payloads.py curls them itself, each the right way (curl()), and draft A was cleared and pasted again at 89142efb; the predictions for the first texts were voided before any check.

A.rendered_check: 226 lines; every line as the rebuild (substack_check_text.py) has it but one, where Substack shows the no-break space of his "Breadcrumbing is" as a plain space; no wrong-way quote mark

B.title: Inner Child, draft B (temp, delete after)

pangram: Both secret links were opened in his Brave through Claude in Chrome, where his Pangram extension labeled each 'Human' and 'Click to view full analysis' was clicked; the full analyses open in tabs outside the session's tab group, so their result pages (pangram.com/feed/...) come from him.
